Definition: properly, something sworn, i.e. an oath
BiblicalUsage: An oath binds the one who swears it. David's covenant reaches back to God's oath unto Isaac, the law settles a dispute between neighbours with an oath of the LORD, and Israel spares the Gibeonites because of the oath which we sware unto them. Zechariah adds the warning: love no false oath, for all these are things that I hate, saith the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that oaths matter because God keeps His. He swore to Abraham and Isaac, and He does not break His word, so I believe my word should be kept too, and a false oath is a small lie told in God's name.
